\section{Alternative methods and their domain of validity}
\label{app:alternative-methods}

Several related methods are useful in restricted circumstances but do not
replace the analytic cut-master calculation described above.

\paragraph{A single global discontinuity.}
The discontinuity of an uncut forward integral sums the physical cuts allowed
in the chosen channel.  It equals a desired multi-particle cut only when a
Cutkosky analysis proves that every other cut is absent or can be separated.
For a general family with several physical cuts, one global discontinuity does
not identify the required cut integral and can combine different phase-space
regions.

\paragraph{Numerical differential equations.}
\AMFlow\ evaluates masters at fixed kinematic points with high precision.  It
is valuable for comparing Laurent coefficients and diagnosing boundary data,
but a collection of fixed-point values does not provide the analytic function
or its endpoint branches.

\paragraph{Direct phase-space integration.}
For linearly reducible parameter densities, direct analytic integration is a
main route and is used in Section~\ref{sec:analytic-masters}.  It becomes less
efficient when several endpoint regions overlap or when a coupled family has
many scales.  Differential equations then reduce the direct integrations to a
smaller set of boundary periods.

\paragraph{A precomputed library of exact masters.}
Known master formulas can shorten a calculation, but they cannot define a
general workflow because the required denominator families are discovered
from the amplitudes.  Whenever a known result is used, its measure, cuts,
branch, and normalization must be mapped explicitly to the family appearing
in the hard coefficient.
